utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Emmerson, I was informed that you'd like to address the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. We have asked Your Honours to come in before the witness is brought in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- simply to seek your guidance on one matter in terms of this witness's proposed evidence-in-chief, and to avoid the need to make objections in the course of the evidence, it seemed sensible to do it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I may cut matters short, the Chamber was informed that there is a part of a statement of this witness which gives second-hand hearsay without giving the sources, that this was dealt with in the proofing notes and that might be your concern, how to elicit this evidence. And I do understand that you were kind enough to draw our attention to part of the transcript, 6th of March, on the matter where you have drawn our attention to what I said at that time, that as to second-hand hearsay evidence or hearsay that's even more remote than that, such evidence, as a rule, does not assist the Chamber and the parties are urged to avoid it as much as possible, keeping in mind that transparency and the flow of information is of greatest importance in relation to such evidence. So if, for whatever reason, you have to rely on it, then please make sure that it's as clear as possible as far as sources are concerned. That's what the Chamber understood. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, the relevant passage was removed from the statement when it was handed to the Chamber. It's set out on the first page of the clip I've handed up to you, and you'll see that it's an allegation, based on rumour, first sentence, "from Albanian friends whose names are not given," and that critically in the penultimate line, "even though they were not eyewitnesses."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So this is second-hand hearsay from an un-named source, which the witness himself describes as rumour. He then comments on that paragraph in his first set of proofing notes. In the first sentence, everything is just hearsay. He says that he spoke to one Albanian and then spoke to another, but it was all based on hearsay. And not simply on hearsay, but as we know from the first statement, hearsay from someone who's not an eye-witness. And as we submit, that as the witness himself points out in the proofing notes, that amounts to speculation by him, another matter which Your Honours discouraged in the guidelines, and Mr. Dutertre has confirmed this morning that the purpose of seeking to elicit this is to put it forward as evidence of the truth of its content. If it were put forward for some other reason, then considerations might be different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We took objection to this passage in an e-mail to the Prosecution on Sunday morning. This witness was proofed again yesterday afternoon, and no further foundation for this has been elicited from him. So it's guidance in respect of that that we'd seek from Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As guidance from the Chamber, the Chamber would not disallow the Prosecution to elicit this evidence, but at the same time the transparency requires that even if this would be in private session, that the witness, at least, gives the names of those who have informed him. Mr. Re -- no, I should say, Mr. Dutertre, that's understood, I take it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I've perfectly understood, and that was the way I intended to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And, of course, you can draw the attention of the witness to the fact that if you're asking questions about his source and names, that he can request to go into private session then. Yes, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I've invited Mr. Dutertre to ensure that he proceeds in stages, in other words, to establish the foundation before seeking to elicit the content.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That would be a reasonable request, I would say. Then, Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours, while the witness is brought in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- could I just raise very, very briefly a matter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- and inform the Trial Chamber we have a new lawyer who will be coming down today, Mr. Phillip Carney, who will be joining the team, and I'll probably introduce him to the Court at the next break when the next witness comes in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it, Mr. Re, that you are delighted to have reinforcement for your team. We'll welcome your new colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Radosevic. I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Dutertre will now continue the examination. [Interpretation] Please proceed, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Radosevic, we'll resume where we stopped yesterday. In essence, you told us that you were stopped by the KLA, that you were arrested and then that you were taken to Glodjane. Just before entering Glodjane, the car of your friend Novak Stijovic broke down, and that's where other soldiers of the KLA arrived and started beating you up. I have the following question: How much time did these beatings last?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stayed there in the street for about an hour before they put us into the room, so we were questioned there in the street for about an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You're talking about a street, but you're actually meaning the road, I suppose?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You just mentioned a street, but you actually mean the road leading to Glodjane, don't you?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's where our car broke down.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And if we go back to my question, how long did the beating last? I understood that you remained for about an hour next to the cars, but how long did they beat you up?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the whole time. While we were there next to the car, we were questioned all the time. All the while we were there on the road, they beat us, so an hour. We would be beaten after every question, regardless of whether we provided an answer or not. We were just beaten up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Was your mother beaten as well?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not beat my mother, but my mother watched all that from a distance of about 2 metres, and she was asking for a glass of water because she had to take a pill. Then one of those people started to curse her Serbian mother, saying, What do you think? And he didn't want to give her a glass of water for her to take this pill. So she went down and there was a puddle on the road, because it had been raining the day before, and so she took some water from this puddle and took this pill.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: When they stopped beating you up, what did happen? You mentioned a room. Can you please tell us what happened next, when they stopped beating you up?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a soldier, I think he was in charge because everybody obeyed him -- they took us to a room 2 metres down from the road. It's a room 3 by 3 metres. And when they took us in there, one of them started beating us up, and the other guy said that we should not be beaten any more, that he was there to interrogate us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You've just described a room. It was a house, I suppose. Can you describe the house and tell us who it belonged to?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know who it belonged to, but as far as I can recall, it was the second or the third house from Rznic to Glodjane, to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You were in that room and you stated that you received blows at the beginning, you were beaten up again. Do you know who beat you up then?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was a soldier from a group of these people who had arrived in two cars and the tractor; one of those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You stated that the one who was in charge intervened, he prevented them from beating you up, and he wanted to interrogate you. What did he ask you?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all kinds of questions, whether I had a rifle, where the police was, where the military was. And they would beat me for any answer I gave. I would be beaten even if I just gave them a phone number. So they asked me all kinds of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: But what did they want, exactly, to know from you?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he wanted us to surrender our weapons. He was asking us about weapons, and Novak and I told him that we didn't have any weapons. I said that my father had weapons because he used to go hunting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: How many weapons did your father possess, and what type of weapons were these?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had two rifles, a hunting -- a shot-gun and a hunting rifle, a carbine rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: When you gave that information to the person who was interrogating you, what did he answer? What did he ask you?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he wanted me to go to the village and to surrender those two rifles, for Novak and myself, and he said that he would kill my mother and my friend if I didn't surrender the two rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You said that you were supposed to go to the village, he wanted you to go to the village. What village is that?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village of Dasinovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: How much time did he give you to go and fetch these weapons?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he gave me half an hour. He gave me half an hour, and I told him that I couldn't make it in half an hour. It was not enough time. And then he said, Well, I'll give you an hour, and then I said I didn't have enough fuel, and then this man said that I could do something to get some fuel. And then I told him that I didn't dare go because they would stop me again and beat me up. And then he gave me the insignia of the Kosovo Liberation Army and said, Well, nobody is allowed to beat you any more today. You just show them this insignia, and nobody will beat you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: If I understand correctly, you've left your mother and your friend with them, and you set off with your car. What route did you take to go to your village of Dasinovac?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I left my mother and my friend in the village of Glodjane, and I went to fetch the hunting rifle. I went to Rznic, then to Gornji Ratis, then from Gornji Ratis to Dasinovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: When you arrived at the family home in Dasinovac, who was there? Who was in your home?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My father Slobodan was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did you tell him what had just happened to you, and did you tell him about the demand made by these KLA soldiers about the weapons?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I told him about it, and he said -- he gave me the carbine, and he said that he was doing that in order for us to get Novak and my mother out alive. And he told me that if I could possibly do that, that I should not go to Glodjane but to Decani to get the other rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And in terms of his own safety, what was your father worried about?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was concerned because of the way I looked, and he was concerned about what would happen to me and my mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: So what did he decide to do about himself?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I told him that there were checkpoints, that they had set up checkpoints everywhere, that the troops were deployed there, holding some kind of a line, and that it was not safe, that he could not move freely. And then he said after nightfall, he would try to get out and go to Decani through the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You left Dasinovac, if I understand correctly, with one weapon in order to go to Decani to retrieve a second weapon there. On your way from Dasinovac to Decani, what happened?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I was going back, in the hamlet of Bandera I was stopped by three persons. I had my rifle with me. One of them was called Caus, and I told him, Caus, this is what happened, my -- our father -- or, rather, my mother and Novak had been captured, and I have to go and surrender this rifle, and I have to go to Decani to get the other one, and he said that he would go with me as far as Pozare to tell them to let me go and to go to Decani to get the other rifle. So I handed over the rifle that I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Do you know the last name, the family name, of this Caus?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure. I think it's Pandja, but I'm not sure. I really am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And where did you meet him for the first time?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'd see him often. He used to work in a company in Decani and, well, he socialised with Serbs.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the last part of his answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the last part of your answer. You said: "He used to work in a company in Decani and, well, he socialised with Serbs." And what did you then say, or is that what you just -- what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that I didn't know his last name. I knew him by sight. I knew that he socialised with Serbs and Albanians. We used to travel together by car, and so we just knew each other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: How old was he, approximately?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, 35, 40. Between 35 and 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Once you reached Pozare, what happened there?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we got to Pozare, he got out of the car and he negotiated with those people to let me through to Decani, to let me get that other rifle. Others -- one group was saying, No, you can't go. Go to Glodjane instead. Another group was in favour of letting me go through to Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: So what was the decision in the end?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, finally, one young man approached me and said, Is it sure that you're going to get that rifle? I said, Yes. He said, What kind of rifle? I said, Automatic rifle. And then this man said, All right. You can go to Decani and get that rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: In Pozare, were they the same soldiers as the ones who stopped you before, or were these other soldiers?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the same group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Did you make use of these -- you had with you. You had mentioned something about an insignia they gave you to show. Did you do that or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the only purpose of that insignia was to stop them from beating me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And just one additional question. What kind of insignia do you mean? Was this a badge or what should we think it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was their badge, a badge of the Kosovo Liberation Army, with the eagle emblem. It was something to be placed on your arm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: So you were allowed to continue your route. So what did you do once you reached Decani?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Decani, I thought of going to the monastery in Decani to try to get my mother and Novak out through their organisation in Pristina. But in the meantime, the policeman from Decani took me to the health centre to stitch up my wound and to have it bandaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did you give the policeman a statement in Decani?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I gave a statement at the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Then what happened to your mother and your friend Novak Stijovic?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I was given that medical assistance, I went to the police station - it was around 14 or 1500 hours - to give that statement, and at that time I was informed that one policeman, on his way to Djakovica from Decani, ran into my mother and Novak walking along the road towards Decani, near the village of Prilep.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Was your mother then taken to Decani together with Novak?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And what did you do after that with your mother?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I couldn't go to Dasinovac village anymore, my uncle Mijo Stesovic came to collect me and to take me to his apartment where I would continue to live.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What happened on the next day?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the morning, I ran into some friends from the village, Slavisa Markovic included, and he said he had come from the village, and that my father had most probably been captured and killed. It happened the evening before.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What had he personally seen or heard about this abduction?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he had a lot of gun-fire, which must have been the attack at my house where my father was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: How far was that from your house?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe a kilometre and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did you give -- did he give some indication about who had abducted your father?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he did. He said it was the KLA, the terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: How did he know that it was the KLA?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, nobody else could have done it because nobody else was allowed to be there; nobody else was allowed to move down there. Only the KLA, especially from the day when I was captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did he tell you what time that was, what time it was when he heard the gun-shots?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said it was 7.00, 7.30, in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And how did he get to Decani, given the presence of the KLA forces all around?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he said so in his statement. Some persons came to his house, friends or I don't know, and took him to Rausici village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What was the ethnicity of these people?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No verbal response].

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: When did you really get to know what had happened to your father?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I found out exactly when I found him, on the 9th of September, but in the meantime I also had news. And in April or early May, on Radio Pristina, it was said that Slobodan Radosevic and Milos Radunovic were found killed along the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You mentioned that this was on the 9th of September you found the body of your father. Who told you about the fact that your father's body had been found?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The policeman from Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zoran Nikic and Vule Mircic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Where did they tell you the body had been found?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said the bodies had been found by the road, near the village of Dasinovac, not far from my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did you go there?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the first day when they had found him because I was unable to go there. I went the next day, and I saw the spot where the bodies had been found, the bodies of Milos Radunovic and my father, Slobodan Radosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: How were you able to locate this spot on the road to Decani? Had you been given specific indications? Were you able to locate it easily?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, since they were residents of Dasinovac village and since I had been told that he was found by the village road, so-called Ninka Road, I looked by the road and it was found. Plus, it was cordoned off by the -- by police tape, the way it's usually done in an on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What do you mean by "cordoned off"?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came there in the morning, by the road on the spot that was indicated to me, scene-of-crime officers had performed an on-site investigation earlier that day, and the spot was marked with yellow police tape before the bodies were taken to Pastrik Hotel for identification and autopsy.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Where is the Pastrik Hotel? Did you go to this hotel, Hotel Pastrik?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went the next day. I couldn't go the same day, but I did go the next day to identify the belongings and to take over the corpse of my father; also to identify him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, from what I think I heard, the witness has answered your question: "Where is the Pastrik Hotel?" However, on the transcript, no answer is recorded. Could you please ask that again?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Radosevic, where is Hotel Pastrik located?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pastrik Hotel is in Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to show the map, which is Exhibit number 10, which we've seen on several occasions yesterday already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Exhibit P10.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Radosevic, could you indicate on this map the route you followed when you came from Glodjane to go to Dasinovac, please, and thereafter could you show us the route you followed from Dasinovac to Decani; thereafter, show us where the village of Prilep is, where your mother and Novak Stijovic were found. Also, could you show us approximately, at any rate, the place where your father's body was found, please?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, could we maybe enhance this map somehow. Maybe zoom in. So since this is a village, that road, that track, it's not drawn into the map, this road by which the bodies were found. Shall I just make a circle around the village itself, the village of Prilep?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Yes, you can draw a circle around the village, please.

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prilep.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Could you then show us - let's do it in the right order - the route you followed between Dasinovac and Decani, on the way back?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to Pozare, the road was an asphalt on. From Pozare on, it was a macadam road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we keep this map aside -- no, can we scroll it and go more to the left so we can see Decani properly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, shall we do it one step by one; that is, you invited the witness, first of all, to indicate where Prilep is. Ask the witness to make the circle as he indicated - I have not seen it yet - and then perhaps add a letter P to that. Could you make a circle where Prilep is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There it is. Yes. I see it's on the map, Prilep. Now, the next step, Mr. Dutertre, you invited the witness to indicate his route from Dasinovac to Decani. Could you please indicate which road --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- runs from Dasinovac to Decani.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Could you indicate the route between Glodjane and Dasinovac and Dasinovac and Decani. Could you mark this with an arrow to show us which direction you were going in, please?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Could you now show us approximately where the body of your father was found; at any rate, where you went and where you saw the area being cordoned off?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't find the scene-of-crime officers there, but approximately here. Maybe the village road is not drawn in, that macadam road I told you about, but it was approximately there by this line.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Could you mark this with a cross? Could you mark it with a cross to indicate the spot where the bodies were found and where you went, the spot where the bodies of Radunovic and Radosevic were found?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to save this map, please, and tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there's no objection, it could immediately be admitted. Madam Registrar, that would be P13, I take it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, you're right. This will be Exhibit number P13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to bring up on the screen the Exhibit number P868, which is a 65 ter document, page 3, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: A 65 ter document?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 868, page 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit number P14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. For the time being, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we enlarge this photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Radosevic, what comments do you have to make, looking at this picture?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a photograph of the spot where my father and Milos Radunovic were found; in fact, their bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document or photograph into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there are no objections, then it's admitted into evidence. I do understand that this picture is one out of a series. Are you intending to enter just this picture or the whole series of pictures?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just this photograph, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Radosevic ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar earlier had in mind to grant -- to attribute P14 to the whole series. She now is limited to this one photograph. And that is tendered and that photograph is now admitted as Exhibit P14. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Radosevic, I'm now about to ask you a number of questions, and I would like you to answer each of my questions and in a precise and accurate manner, and please do not go beyond my questions when you answer them. Could you at least provide a short answer in the first case? Now, after that, did you hear anything about what had happened to your father; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Pardon? What do you mean by "after that"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can I still ask questions to the witness as to the content of the information given by this individual? Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Radosevic, what did this friend tell you precisely on the abduction and death of your father?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he told me that he had been captured by the KLA and taken to the village of Glodjane, and that he had tried to protect them but that he had been beaten for his efforts to protect Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we, in this part of the evidence, could you insist that the witness always clearly describes -- for example, if he says that he told me that he had been captured, that the witness gives us details of what was told to him; for example, that he told you that he was present when he was captured or was not present when he was captured. We'd like to know exactly what your friend observed himself and what, possibly, he has heard from others or whether he got information from any other person. So could you please be very precise in that respect. So could you please restart your answer where you said that: "He told me that he had been captured by the KLA." Did he tell you that your friend was present when your father was captured by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, he was not there on site when he had been captured. When they headed to Glodjane, when they passed by his house, he went out and, most probably, he stopped them and tried to save the two of them. Well, probably he had been beaten. I don't know how they influenced him. But he said that he had been beaten. So when he had been captured, when they headed from my house towards Glodjane, he stopped there. He stood in the road, maybe 5 or 6 metres down the road, and he just stopped them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You mention two individuals. Did he give you the names of these two people? I understood your father was there. Did he give you the name of the other person?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Milos Radunovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What did he say to the soldiers when he stopped them on the road? What was the content of what he said to the soldiers? Did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he didn't tell me in so many words what he had told the soldiers. He went out and he said that they should let them go, that Slobodan Radosevic and Milos Radunovic did not deserve this kind of fate, for them to take them and to abuse them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: When he stopped them, did he tell you what means of transportation they were using, Milos Radunovic and Slobodan, your father?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he said that it was by car, but he didn't specify the make. And he said that the persons, the soldiers, were not from the village of Dasinovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: How many cars were they? Did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What were the names of the soldiers who were taking your father and Milos Radunovic? Did he know these men? Did he tell you who they were?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he didn't tell me specifically who they were. He only told me that they were not from the village of Dasinovac. The locals were not involved in my father's kidnapping.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Who is Deli Lekaj? Do you know that individual? Deli Lekaj; do you know that individual?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know him by sight. I heard that he had been in the Kosovo Liberation Army at the time when Vesko Stijovic had been arrested, Dragoslav Stojanovic and Kika Stojanovic, when they were all arrested. I heard rumours that he had participated in the murder of my father, but I can't say that for sure because I, myself, did not see it. So that I don't have the exact information that would point to the fact that he killed my father, but I do have some information indicating that he did participate in the murder of my father.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, I'd like to seek to clarify. You first said you heard rumours. Later, you said you do have some information. Do you have any information which goes beyond rumours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honour, I know that Delija Lekaj participated in the capture of Vesko Stijovic, Dragoslav Stojanovic and Kika Stojanovic, but I heard the rumour, I did not have the exact information. I heard the rumour that he participated in the arrest of my father.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So it's -- the information is, at this moment, just rumour. Now you told us that you know that he participated in the capture of the other people you mentioned; that is, Mr. Stijovic and two Stojanovics. Have you seen that? Have you -- what's the source of your knowledge in relation to the capture of these persons and the involvement of Mr. Lekaj in that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. Vesko Stijovic is a close family friend of ours. He told me about this whole incident when he was captured and how he was interrogated and what kind of advice he was given. So I heard it from Vesko Stijovic, Dragoslav and Kika Stojanovic, that this man had been in the Kosovo Liberation Army in Glodjane at the time of their arrest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And also that he was involved; that this man was involved in their arrest, or ...?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That he was involved in their arrest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Once more, which man are we talking about? Can you repeat the name, who was involved in the arrest, according to what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Delija Lekaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did your friend describe the physical condition of Milos Radunovic and of your father, Slobodan Radosevic, when he stopped the UCK soldiers taking these two persons?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he said that they had been beaten up. He couldn't see very clearly whether they were injured or not. They had been beaten up. At any rate, he told me that they were alive when they were taken to Glodjane.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: How did he describe the blows that he received himself?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they punched him for defending the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Let me go back a little. How many soldiers were they when he stopped them to try and save your father, as well as Milos Radunovic?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from what he told me, they were in two cars, so maybe seven or eight of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And your friend was adamant that these were UCK soldiers?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You said that he told you that they left towards Glodjane. How could he know that they were heading towards Glodjane?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the same as when we were arrested. Whatever happened, whoever was arrested by the KLA, they would be taken to the headquarters in Glodjane where they were interrogated and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: To be more specific, you said there were two cars. In which direction did those two cars go?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they headed from Dasinovac to Pozare, where they probably took a turn to Glodjane.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: He observed all this himself. Did he tell you anything else?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he said that he had heard a rumour that the two of them had been killed later and thrown by the road near the Linkin Put location and that they were up there, and then maybe three or four months later he went there to check whether that was really true. He took a shovel with him, and then he just threw some soil over them. They were already decomposed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did he give you any names of people who had committed the murder of your father and of Milos Radunovic?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And you yourself, did you find out anything else about the circumstances of these deaths?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I heard rumours that they had been taken to Glodjane; that they had been questioned there; that Milos Radunovic was wounded in the hand, Slobodan Radosevic in his leg; that they were taken to Prilep village to be taken on to Decani. In the Prilep village, the villagers said, Don't leave them there; otherwise, we could be blamed for it. So they were taken back to Dasinovac village, and they were killed there, or maybe they were left to bleed to death.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You're now talking about rumours which are -- sometimes rumours can play a role in evidence; for example, if you said your friend heard by rumours that your father's body was thrown at the side of the road and that made him look for it, then the rumour is the reason why he went there. Here you're talking about the substance. If you have no further information about the source of these rumours, then I would invite Mr. Dutertre to move on to his next subject, because you'll understand, in a court of law, rumours can play only a very limited role, as I just explained to you. Mr. Dutertre, I'm also looking at the clock at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am almost at the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Radosevic, did you give another statement to other people about what happened to you?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave statements to journalists. I gave a statement at the monastery, I don't know which organisation exactly it was, but I gave that statement in the monastery of Decani concerning what had happened to me and my mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You mentioned an organisation. Did I understand you correctly? You were questioned by an organisation, but it was not anything related to the police?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was an organisation but I can't remember which. Some sort of organisation, yes, I do remember that, but which one I can't recall now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What did you tell them precisely?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I told them that -- I told them everything that had happened to me that day, how I was captured, where I was taken, what I was forced to do, how we were mistreated and abused. I told them also I had heard on the radio that my father was left lying by the road, or his body, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to show Exhibit number 5. It's an exhibit already. And I'd like to have a look at pages 14 and 15 of that exhibit. That's the English version of the document, but yesterday we provided a translation of this document in Serbian to all Defence teams. They will correct me if I'm wrong. And I also believe that this document has been uploaded into the e-court system. But I'd like the original Serb versions to be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that you're referring to P5.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could the Serbian version be enlarged on the screen so the witness can -- yes, that very much seems to be the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Radosevic, can you please read -- have a look at this document and make comments about this document, if you have any.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry to rise to my feet. I think there may be some confusion between P5 and P6. I understand Mr. Dutertre intends to put to this witness his own statement, but I think on the system what is coming up is, at least in English, a statement made by a different witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At the same time, if I look at the translation, I see that on the top we find K057 and then 7181, and then K057 and then 7182. However, on the translation, I find K057-7193, which seems to be a different document, but I'm not quite sure what has happened here. But I see that the numbers are not corresponding.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. The translation is for e14glodj.doc which is the correct reference for the translation of this witness's HLC statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The reference that Mr. Dutertre has given is to e20glodj.doc, which is a different witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Dutertre, could you help us out?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I asked for the following document to be displayed: Pages 14 and 15, K057-7121.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure of the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And on your screen, you have not the right document. We should have 7181 and not 7193.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see that e20glodj.doc is on the screen, whereas we are -- we want to look at, which is a bit of an odd number, that it's "e" small "i4," but I take it that's for e14, which is --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's a mis-transcription. The document that Mr. Dutertre is looking for is e14glodj.doc.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, we have now got the English and the right versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, here we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Radosevic, could you please comment on this document for us, please?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's the statement that I gave at the monastery to that organisation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could we have the second microphone turned on for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Are there any corrections you'd like to make or anything else you would like to say about this page?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have nothing to add.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we move on to the next page both in English and in Serbian, and here we find the heart of the statement, the substance of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Radosevic, can you please have a look at this document and comment on it in any way you see fit.

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's the statement that I gave that day at the monastery to that organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Any comments about this document, if you've read it?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have a comment to make to the very statement, the introductory part.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Can you please make that comment?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it says here that I had run away; in fact, that they turned up in our village on the 21st of April, the Kosovo Liberation Army, and that I fled with my mother and friend to the youth camp in Decani. We didn't flee at all. That day I was taken, I was taking my mother to see a doctor, and we spent the night in Decani, and I tried to go back to my village but I was captured instead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to read the whole of your statement right now or did you just read the beginning of it? Otherwise, I'd suggest that we'll have a break now and that the witness will be provided with a copy in his own language of the statement so that he has an opportunity to review it during the break. Is there any hard copy available in Serbian for the witness? Yes, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Here we have a translation and attached to it we have the translation of the last document I wanted to use, extracted from Exhibit P6. So I do not know whether you want to give him both these translations now or only the translation of the document we are currently dealing with.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'd like an opportunity to see what it is that Mr. Dutertre wishes the witness to read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please show it to Mr. Emmerson, because P5 is clear now but P6, then ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit P6, that's a "Spotlight" report, number 26, and I'm interested in pages 18 and 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Having reviewed it, the last page - it might help the witness to know this - the last page is, in fact, a separate document. What it is is a translation into Serbian of an extract of "Spotlight" report 26, one of the reports which we've already had exhibited. If the witness doesn't realise that, it might very well be misleading. So if they could be pulled apart on the staple so he knows he's looking at two different documents, and I certainly have no objection to him looking at either of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Radosevic, you will be provided with two documents in your own language. The one is the document you just saw on the screen, which I invite you to read carefully over the break to see whether there are any further comments you'd like to make. And then you'll also be provided with another document, but that document is not -- does not reflect any statement of you, but it's a part of a report. I'd like you to read that as well, and then we'll see what questions Mr. Dutertre might have on that. Could it be given to the witness in his own language? Yes. Then I'd like you, Mr. Radosevic, to follow Mr. Usher and leave the courtroom, read that. We'll have a break for a little bit less than half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Dutertre, we spent now approximately two and three-quarters of an hour on the testimony of a witness which was scheduled for one hour, and of course I wondered. We have maps saying exactly that he went from A to B on the road which is, I would say, the road you take because it's the direct road between A and B. We have now detailed information that the witness's mother was finally found in Prilep. Of course, it could be that it has some very specific importance, but until now it could have been any village in the area, if not too far away from Decani and somewhere in the area. You spent a lot of time on these kind of things, where I even wonder, apart from how relevant it is to receive this information but perhaps it turns out to be of vital importance, but also I've asked myself whether or not 80 per cent of this information could have been led through 89(F) or in whatever other way, by just referring to the written statement. Of course, we do not know yet what will be the real important points on cross-examination, but at least the question came into my mind and it might not have come into my mind if you would have finished this witness's examination-in-chief within one hour, but since it has taken now almost three hours, that question certainly came into my mind. We will -- and, Mr. Emmerson, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I was on my feet on another matter, but I should say, in fairness to Mr. Dutertre, the amount of material with this witness that could have been dealt with, so to speak, by agreement or by reading as part of the overall description is comparatively limited. I have questions for him which cover --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, then, I might have been -- my concern still is two and three-quarters of an hour, but perhaps on the substance I should have waited until a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The other concern I have is that, for reasons I'm not entirely sure about, we now have e12glodj.doc and a translation on the screen. Now, I don't know whether there's a reason for that or it's in any way found its way into the records, but there's something going wrong with these documents. That's nothing whatever to do with this testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know whether it's recorded, what is on the screen. Yes, I think it is. It has been shown. But e12 at this moment has not been -- at least, we did not read anything from that. We'll adjourn and resume at a quarter past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Radosevic, did you have an opportunity to read the documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then Mr. Dutertre might have questions for you. Please proceed, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you very much. I will be very brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Do you have any comments to make, any additions to what is stated in these documents, Mr. Radosevic?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I want to say that in the introductory part of this one statement, what is written is not exactly what I said. It's not the way it happened. It was not recorded correctly. It was not recorded as I put it, as I stated it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Radosevic, can you please tell us specifically what document you have in mind? There should be a number on this document on the top right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's document 71H2003.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Do you mean the correction you already told us before about the reason to travel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: So we don't have to repeat that, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Anything else you would like to add related to this document?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing else. Everything is as stated in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Radosevic, now about the second document, P6, pages 18 and 19 in the English version. This is a one-page document that was given to you together with the other documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Maybe it's better to stay with this document we just saw before, and that saves time because we then don't have to go back to this. I just wanted to understand better. This was an interview or a statement you gave a couple of days after that incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Good. And that was a time when you didn't yet have any clear news about the fate of your father. Do I understand that correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: You had heard -- in fact, you told us before, on that same evening in the place, in your village or in where? You heard something about a rumour that your father was abducted and killed, or you say here different stories. "Some say he was wounded; others, that he was killed." So I wanted to know: What did you do after that first stories you had heard, on the same evening? Did you go, then, to the place? Had you been, then, looking for your father? Because we jumped to September, when you found the body, when the body was found, but I wanted to know what you did in the beginning to find out about your father. Can you give us information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it happened the next morning. After I was captured, Slavisa Markovic came with his family from Dasinovac village. His neighbours took him out up to Rausivac village. So my father was captured at his own threshold by the terrorists, and I lived in the hope that he was still alive to the last day, to the 9th of September. I didn't really trust the rumours that he was dead or wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: So, once more, the last time you saw your father was when you went for the hunting rifles; yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And you heard something that same evening or next morning about him having been captured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And then what did you do about that? Did you try to find out more?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tried. I tried through the monastery to look into it and find out if they could find out through NGOs, but I didn't manage to find out anything. Then I heard on the news about their fate. I didn't believe it, I didn't believe they were lying by the road. My sister tried in Podgorica. She went to the Red Cross to try to check out that information that was on the news bulletin that they were lying by the road, and they apparently went there to check it out but apparently they didn't find them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And was police involved? Did you involve police in one way or the other? And did police investigate at your house in your village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I reported it the same day to the police, the same day when I was captured. As soon as I was released, I and Slavisa Markovic went to the police to give a statement, but the police couldn't go to my village because it was blocked by the terrorist army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one clarifying question, I'm seeking clarification. You had no further comments on the statement, you said. Now, in the statement a description is given which includes the breakdown of Novak's car, and then a little bit later, it says that they were punching and hitting you. "It was around noon. They didn't hit my mother, but they gave me and Novak a proper beating. Right there, in the middle of the road." And then it continues: "At about 2 p.m., they decided to let us go and towed our car to Prilep." That's not -- you say you have no further comments, but your testimony in this court was quite different from that, not that at about 2 p.m. they decided to let you go, but they said you had to go and find the rifles, the weapons, they kept your mother more or less as a hostage, and -- so that story, to that extent, it surprises me that you have no further comments because these are two stories which are not the same.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Your Honour, if I omitted anything. But about this statement, about what you're saying, it's true that it's written there. I stand by that first statement that I gave to these gentlemen here as to what happened, how the car broke down, how we were captured, mistreated, abused, beaten; that I went to Dasinovac to get that rifle, that I turned it over, surrendered it, in Pozare village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you're saying not only the beginning of the statement is not recording, as you said, what you told them, but the end of the recording, at least, does not reflect what you testified in this courtroom, and you say that what you said in this courtroom is what happened, if it deviates from anything said in this written statement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I stand by my first statement that I gave. That's the statement that I signed. This is a statement made by an NGO. They could have put all kinds of stuff in there. It is correct that I was captured, but it's not true that I ran away from the village. I went with my mother to Decani for her to see a doctor. I was captured on our way back. I was not released by the terrorists in the village of Prilep, nor was my mother released in Prilep. And they towed their car there to Prilep by tractor and left them there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: One follow-up question. When did you see first this statement as it is recorded here? Did you first see this statement here in court, or were you presented with this statement at an earlier stage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I saw this statement yesterday. Yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: In court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: So it follows from that, you were never given any opportunities to comment on this -- what is recorded here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. Really, I had not seen this statement before yesterday, so let me say it once again: It is correct that I was captured and all that, but it is not true that I was released in Prilep by the KLA. I was forced to surrender my rifle, and my friend and my mother were released in Prilep.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may, Your Honour -- Your Honours, this document was shown to Mr. Radosevic during the proofing session. He did give us his comments, as is reflected in the proofing notes, and he did mention a number of things which he's just mentioned here today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to bring up on the screen Exhibit P6, and more specifically pages 18 and 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Radosevic, on the right-hand side, you have the translation of pages 18 and 19; on the left-hand side, you have page 18, and we shall enlarge page 18. What I'm interested in is what is located on the fifth paragraph of this page. Do you have any comments to give us as regards this document?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do have some amendments. My mother and myself went on the 21st of April to Decani, from my village to Decani, that's what I said already, for her to see her doctor. And then the next day, I headed with my mother back to the village, and that's where -- when we were captured. That's clear from the other statement. So it is true that I left the village with my mother, and my father stayed in the village. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: But this was on the 21st of April, was it?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. At the bottom of this page, if we turn to the last paragraph, do you have any comments to make as regards this particular paragraph?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing related to this paragraph. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: I'd like to clarify something -- or question, rather. This was Novak's rifle, Novak's father's rifle, that you were walking around with or was it your father's rifle? The paragraph states that at around a quarter past 2.00, you returned to the headquarters of the KLA, carrying with you Novak's rifle.

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I went there with the carbine that belonged to my late father, to the village of Pozare, where Caus took the carbine, and I wasn't able to find Novak's father's carbine. So I never went back to the village of Glodjane, but I went to Decani in order purportedly to get the other rifle because I was told to get two rifles. So I never went back to Glodjane, I went straight to Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we could turn to page 19 now, please. We still have the translation up on the screen. I'm referring to the first two paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You have the translation on the bottom right-hand side in your version. Do you have any comments to make here?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I'm receiving any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: The translation should be on one of the pages which is up on the screen. It's the bottom part of the document. The translation is on the same page in your version. This was given to you during the break.

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two paragraphs about the disappearance of Slobodan Radosevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I stand by this. It's just the first paragraph. I said that on the 21st of April, I had gone with my mother to Decani for her to see her doctor. We spent the night there, and in the morning we went back to the village. So I state that once again. The second paragraph is fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Radosevic. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to inform the Chamber that the scale of the map we have used is 1:100.000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I -- sooner or later, then, we'll hear what is the scale of the other map. I mean, the scale is indicated as 1:100.000. What makes you so sure about that it has never been enlarged or reduced in size?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The map we have been using all the time is 1:100.000, and that is the information that was communicated to me by the investigators through the Map Unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yesterday, I referred to map number 6, which is not in evidence but which was provided to us at an early stage, which seems to be the same map, although marked with some red circles on it. And at the bottom of that map, which is clearly not the same scale, it also says it's 1:100.000. This one -- I'm thinking about ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The map we have been using is map number 7, the one which we have been showing throughout.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's clear to me. So you're saying the -- of course, it's the same map, although reduced -- or enlarged or the other one is reduced. So either one of the two is not indicating the right scale or, perhaps, even both of them are not indicating the right scale dependent on what is the original map, because on the original map we find the scale which allows us to see what distances are. I have other maps. I'll verify myself, on the basis of all the material, whether this information -- whether it's correct that 7 still is the original size. That's not difficult to do. I'll do that on the basis of maps with the scale indicated on the map themselves, because there you can compare. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we shall try and give you a map tomorrow containing the scale we have just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll wait and see what we receive. No further questions for the witness. Then, Mr. Emmerson, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Radosevic, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Emmerson, who is counsel for Mr. Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Radosevic, you've told us that at the time of this incident in April, when you were stopped at the crossroads in Pozhare, you were working as a security guard at a refugee camp; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the people that you were guarding there were, by and large, Serbs; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The people who were housed there were Serbs, but in the company where I worked, the composition was mixed; there were Serbs and Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was there an armed guard at the camp?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: How long did you work there?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four years.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When did you leave your employment at the camp?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1998/1999, when those persons were put in the village of Junik and Labovic, when they got their own homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so you remained working there right the way through the whole of 1998, did you?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Going back to the incident on the 21st/22nd, I just want to look at some of the background questions with you, first of all. I think that you had rented a room in Decan for yourself to live in, in order to be closer to work; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. The room was there in the company. So when the weather was bad, I could sleep there in order not to have to go home.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And your brother -- you have a brother called - forgive my pronunciation if I get it wrong - Radoje? Radoje is your brother?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He'd also left Dashinoc in order to move to Peje where he lived and worked; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Can you help us? Did he not live and work in Peje at all?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He did not work in Pec, he worked in a company in Decani.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't get the name of the company.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So he worked in a company in Decani. Where was he living?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up until one month before this situation came up, he lived in Decani. So that's when he left. His company closed down. He went to Budvar to lay parquet floors. That's what he had been doing in the previous company, but now he went to Budvar to do that for a privately owned business.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Neither of you had left Dashinoc in fear of the KLA, had you?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we didn't leave it in fear of the KLA. I cannot say anything bad about our neighbours. Our neighbours were good. We heard from the news that they would walk around at night, but during the day the situation was normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, excuse me, are you speaking of Dasinovac?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: It says --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Dashinoc is the Albanian pronunciation; Dasinovac is the Serbian. I'm happy to use either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: No, no, no. I don't know about the pronunciation in the Albanian version, Dashinoc or something --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, Dashinoc.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Okay. So, please, we're speaking of the same village?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I mean if from time to time, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: It's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There's no significance to be attached to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The point is, Mr. Radosevic, you hadn't seen yourself any evidence of the KLA in your village before this incident, had you?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not in my village. But I went to see my friend Culafic, whose house had been shelled, but in my village nothing was noticeable.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And can I ask you this: Was that also a pattern in other villages, that younger people left the countryside to live and work in the larger towns? Other people that you knew of your own generation had left the countryside villages quite often to live and work in the larger towns?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't really give you an answer to that question. I'm not interested in other villages. What I'm interested in is my own, my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know the Vlahovics from Ratis?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the male members of the family of around your age, had they also moved away to work elsewhere at this point?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just tell you one thing: All of us worked in Pec or in Decani, but we all went back to our homes to sleep there and to spend time there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We know that your mother spent the night of the 21st, that is to say, the night before this incident occurred, with you in Decan because she was going to the doctor; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And we've looked, obviously, at the extracts from the report that you've seen, as well as the statement that you are recorded as having made to the NGO. The descriptions given there are wrong about this, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me repeat once again: There are things here that actually did happen, but let me say once again: The correct statement is the one that I signed. They could have written down anything they wanted. So I stand by the statement that I signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that, but you are recorded as having told the lady from the NGO that you had fled your village in fear of the KLA. And I think you're telling us that you never said that to her; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, if I had not fled, I would have been dead. I had to flee. At one point, I handed over the rifle and I fled. They did not let me go of their own free will.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Radosevic, the statement you made to the NGO, which you've got in front of you in Serbian, begins by a statement that says that you left Dashinoc with your mother and your friend Novak and fled to a youth camp in Decani after the KLA turned up in your village on the 21st of April. Now, you've told us that's not true, is it? It's not true?

utterances.speaker: STANISA RADOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, let me make this quite clear, once again: The journalists and the NGOs, they can write whatever they please. I stand by my statement. On the 21st of April, I took my mother to see her doctor.
